short: The United States Army detonated the world's first nuclear device in the New Mexico desert, validating the plutonium implosion design.
full:
On 16 July 1945, scientists and military personnel of the Manhattan Project detonated an implosion-design plutonium device, nicknamed 'The Gadget', at the Alamogordo Bombing and Gunnery Range in the Jornada del Muerto desert of New Mexico. The explosion yielded an energy equivalent of approximately 21 kilotons of TNT, instantly vaporising the steel test tower and fusing the desert sand into a mildly radioactive green glass called trinitite. The test proved that the highly complex implosion mechanism required for a plutonium bomb was functional.

The successful detonation was immediately communicated to President Harry S. Truman, who was attending the Potsdam Conference, significantly bolstering his negotiating position against the Soviet Union. Three weeks after the Trinity test, an identical plutonium bomb named 'Fat Man' was dropped on the Japanese city of Nagasaki, ensuring the end of the Second World War and launching the atomic age.
